sections.title: What’s Included
sections.body:
All Tiers include a monthly letter which includes:

  • postcard
  • a handwritten letter
  • a rotating monthly bonus goody

Each month, I will share what I am thinking about and learning, a silly poem I have loved or written, or ways to live intentionally and enjoy life.

One Time Payment – $12

Monthly Subscription – $10

Bonus birthday letter

Yearly Subscription – $110

One month free + Bonus Birthday

As a subscriber, you can determine where your dollars go by dividing your 50% into equal parts or allocating it to whichever you would like to fund.

Financial transparency is a key value of Dream-Rock and will be updated quarterly as the mail club grows.

sections.title: We All We Got SD
sections.body:
Food and resource distribution throughout San Diego county

Mutual aid is about solidarity, not charity

  • Food distribution serving 300 families per month
  • Migrant Aid providing 5-100 meals per day
  • Resource center for community needs throughout San Diego

sections.title: Indigenous Climate Action
sections.body:
Indigenous-led organization guided by knowledge keepers, water & land defenders from communities and regions across the country.

a) Strategic disruption of harmful colonial practices, policies, and processes and amplify Indigenous modalities of creative expression and storytelling;

b) Nurturing community members through understandings of healing justice, community engagement, and strategic climate education and training;

c) Exploring new climate solutions with community members at the grassroots, grasstops, and in elected leadership that center Indigenous values to imagine and create a just future.

sections.title: Otay Mesa Detention Resistance
sections.body:
Organizing against the inhumane detentions and human rights abuses at Otay Mesa Detention Center.

The three areas of focus:

  • Supporting people in detention centers by funding phone calls, contacting family outside, transporting them, and organizing their post-release support
  • Supporting people once released
  • Advocacy, researching federal, state, and local policies, and trainings.

sections.title: About Dream-Rock Collective
sections.body:
I believe in the power of creativity and imagination, and in the collective power of everyday, average people. Merging the power of art with community reinvestment, Dream-Rock Collective focuses on actively creating the world we want to live in.

We are donating 50% of our profits to local mutual aids and nonprofits that can do the work in impacted and under-invested communities.

50% of profits towards:

  • Food Distribution
  • Climate Justice
  • Supporting neighbors impacted by ICE

As a subscriber, you can determine where your dollars go dividing up your 50% in equal parts, or whichever you would like to fund.

Financial transparency is a key value of Dream-Rock, and will be updated quarterly as the mail club grows.

sections.title: About the Artist
sections.body:
Leeya Appleby was raised in Hawaii and has lived in San Diego, California, for her entire adult life. She has a BA in Philosophy, a BA in Psychology, and a Master’s in Peace Studies and Social Justice. She loves to read and write about nature and is always learning more about what it means to be alive in this particular time.

Leeya is an oil painter, print-maker, and collage artist. Her subjects focus on romanticizing the magic of everyday life and art activism focused on climate justice and human rights. Leeya often creates art around the experience of being gay and neurodivergent—capturing the joy and complexities that come with being alive.
